newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GOVT TO AMEND BUDGET BILL TO MATCH TAX CUT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GOVT TO AMEND BUDGET BILL TO MATCH TAX CUT.

text.p: Poland's finance minister said on Friday he will soon amend his 1997 budget draft to take into account the Senate's personal income tax cut, which will up the budget gap to 2.8 percent of GDP from the planned 2.6 percent.
"A tax solution proposed by the Senate is close to that of the government. We will soon propose relevant changes in the budget draft," Kolodko told a news conference.
On Thursday, the Senate lowered next year's personal income tax levels to 20, 32 and 44 percent from the current 21, 33 and 45 percent, which will cost the budget about 180 million in lost revnues.

The Senate also rejected an even deeper tax cut, to 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent, suprisingly proposed by the lower house as a result of bickering in the ruling leftist coalition, which Kolodko said would have thrown public finance into chaos.
Kolodko, who had himself earlier suggested a tax cut to 20, 31 and 43 percent, said he was confident the lower house would now approve the senate's tax proposal at a session next week.

Kolodko's budget draft, submitted to parliament last month, assumed that next year's personal tax levels would be the same as in 1996 because the government was unsure of the outcome of the tax debate in parliament.
The deficit envisaged by the draft was therefore set at 2.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Kolodko confirmed his earlier statement that the 0.2 point deficit adjustment would be financed in a non-inflationary way but did not give any details.
He also said he was finishing work on a bill that would transfer more funds to local authorities from the central government as off next year.
Under the planned regulation, local governments would receive 16 percent of revenues from the personal income tax and not 15 percent as it is the case now.
